content.prompt: This diagram represents a river (shaded) with a tree on the bank at point A. A man stands directly opposite A, on the opposite bank, at point B. He then walks 100 m along the bank, to point C, where he places a peg. He then walks a further 50 m to point D, turns 90° and walks 65 m to point E, where he finds that E,C and A are in a straight line. Find the width of the river.

spec.description: Actual shaded river strip, perpendicularAB/DE, D-C-B collinear withBC100/CD50 in stem; E-C-Acollinear withDE65. Exact common physical scale, no derived width given.
spec.mathematics: Actual shaded river strip, perpendicularAB/DE, D-C-B collinear withBC100/CD50 in stem; E-C-Acollinear withDE65. Exact common physical scale, no derived width given.
spec.answerVisibility: Original givens only; all computed values remain in answers.

answer.worked: Triangles ABC and EDC are right-angled at B and D, and their angles at C are vertically opposite, so they are similar by AAA. Thus $\frac{AB}{DE}=\frac{BC}{DC}=\frac{100}{50}=2$. Therefore the river width is $AB=2(65)=130\text{ m}$.
